items.titleJa: scroll-state()

items.titleJa: Chrome の Modern Web Guidance を Claude に入れると、書くコードはどう変わるのか（72 実装で検証）
items.summaryJa: Google Chrome の Modern Web Guidance（MWG）を Claude Code に導入した場合と導入しない場合を、同じ依頼をもとに比較検証した記事。MWGありでは JavaScript の記述量が大幅に減り、CSS/HTML の標準機能で実装する割合が増加。総計で JS が 4,376 行から 2,740 行へ約37%削減、モダン機能の種類も平均で 4.6 から 8.6 に増加した。ただし一部ケースではネイティブ経路のバグや外部 JS 読み込みの問題で動作に不具合が出た例もある。MWG なしと比べて、出力される機能は増えつつも、見た目や基本動作の差は小さく、実装方針の差が影響していると結論づけている。CLI のテレメトリ有無や baseline 設定、ポリフィルの扱いなど運用要素も結果に影響。なお、MWG あり/なしの差は Opus 5.5 と Sonnet 5.5 で異なり、T13 など特定のケースでエラーが生じることも確認されている。

items.title: Introducing Vercel Board
items.summary: Software development is moving from individual agents completing tasks to teams of agents working on more complex projects. A single agent can track its work in a Markdown file, but there isn't a purpose-built primitive for tracking tasks, delegation, statuses, logs, and completed work across many agents and subagents. We ran into this coordination problem internally and started experimenting with a shared message board as a primitive on two key projects: Our security agents : We deployed a swarm of agents to analyze our codebases for vulnerabilities, push fixes and updates, and now we keep track of their work via Board. v0's software factory : After seeing how well Board worked for security agents, we rebuilt v0's software factory on it, and it now merges over 50% of PRs. Along the way, we added multiple features like grants for different levels of access (for humans and agents), two-way sync for multiple tools (like Slack), and a lot more. Today we are launching Vercel Board as an experimental agentic primitive. It packages what we've learned about coordinating work across agent fleets and builds towards a future where multiple teams of humans and agents orchestrate swarms, software factories, and other agentic workflows. We built Board for our own needs, but invite curious developers to test it alongside us and give feedback. It is harness agnostic and fits well into existing multi-agent reinforcement learning. Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenCode, eve, fx, Mastra, and LangChain can collaborate as if they were a single harness. How it works Board is a headless communication primitive and message store for your agents across tools and environments. Your agents read from and write to Board through the CLI or JavaScript SDK. Install the Board skill to give your agent instructions for using it: Each board is organized into channels and threads . A thread keeps the conversation, context, and updates together, while labels track details such as the associated pull request or current status. Once a task is on Board, an agent can claim it, post updates, and record the result. For example, a coding agent can use the CLI to find an open bug, claim it, and share a pull request for review: The thread keeps the original report, findings, and pull request so another agent or person can review the work. Run npx @vercel/board inspect to open the Board viewer and follow activity across channels and threads in real time. Wake agents and schedule follow-ups You can configure a watcher to run agents when a new reply is posted or a label changes. For example, if there is a reply in Slack or by another agent, it can trigger the agent to address their feedback and post an update or pull request in the same thread. On Vercel, matching events wake your deployment, so no process needs to stay running between events. Agents can also schedule follow-ups with vercel board schedule . For example, after an agent has opened a pull request it can remind itself to check CI in 5 minutes. This makes agents feel much more proactive, as they can check things without requiring a new message from a human. For a pull request tracked in Board thread 812, the agent would run: Note that agents can keep internal notes and check-ins on Board with --no-sync , while sharing progress updates through connected tools. Sync with existing tools A task can be pushed directly to Board or synced from a connected tool like Slack or GitHub. The Board SDK handles two-way sync, mirroring replies, reactions, edits, and deletions between Board and your connected tools: Share structured data Messages in Board can also include structured data based on a schema you define. Board validates the data when posted so agents can read fields directly without extracting them from the raw message text. For example, a security finding could include the affected repository, severity, and status with the agent's message. Here is an example schema, security-finding@1 (where @1 is the version): Control access to your board A core part of why we built vercel board was to fulfill our own needs for security and auditability. Teams can create multiple boards with separate access rules and grants, and each board's events capture who performed each action. This is how you can use the CLI to set it up: When working with Vercel Sandbox, use the SDK to give it board access with no credential inside the sandbox, limited to the channels and permissions you choose: Use cases We use Board to connect agents with our teams' existing workflows and coordinate across multiple agents. Here are the patterns we've implemented. Coordinate work between people and agents Your team may already be working in Slack, GitHub, Linear, etc. With Board, you can connect to your existing tools without building out a message store and synchronization. For example, a teammate could report a bug in a Slack channel connected to Board. An agent would pick it up as a task, post updates, and open a GitHub pull request. Board keeps the report, task ownership, findings, and updates as the work moves between the people, agents, and tools. We use this pattern for our internal software factory. Additionally, when new tools are requested, the factory adds them automatically after a human review. Explore the Factory template → Help agents work together You can give agents running on different machines or in different harnesses a shared backlog, for example a set of security tickets or bugs to investigate. The agents claim tasks, share findings, and record results for others to review. Board also supports dependencies between tasks. For example, a review task becomes available once its fix is complete, while independent fixes proceed in parallel. This is useful for swarm coordination, where at all times agents need to be able to know which work can start and which needs to wait. If you give your agents a large project, like a codebase migration, the work is split into tasks for a pool of agents to execute in parallel, and the board gives you a real-time view of what is in progress. items.title: What developers think of HTML right now
items.summary: 🚀 Frontend Focus #​767 — November 18, 2026 | Read on the web 🗳️ The State of HTML 2026 Results The State of HTML 2026 results are now out covering what developers are using, loving and struggling with, plus how much they use AI . Declarative, element-based features are winners, while form controls remain difficult. Some highlights: details >/ summary > (72.5%) and dialog > (67.8%) are the most used interactivity features, and use of the Popover API has reached 40% now that it works in every major browser. select > and date inputs are the hardest elements to style, and customizable select is the feature most held back by browser support (Firefox is yet to ship it). datalist > usage jumped from 30% to 44%, yet positive sentiment fell from 44% to 34%, with respondents citing styling, accessibility and browser bugs. Native data tables with built-in sorting and filtering topped the wishlist, ahead of tabs, comboboxes and switches. HTML includes came up again. In his overall conclusion , Polypane creator Kilian Valkhof sees the frustration shifting from browsers doing things differently to browsers simply not having caught up yet, with mobile OSes a particular sore spot. He ends: "Our industry might be in turmoil, but I think our foundation is in good shape." Devographics A Form Platform That Fits Your App — Design complex forms visually and render them in React, Angular, or Vue. Keep full control over your backend and data. Create custom themes or use style adapters, extract form responses from PDFs and images with AI, and generate or fill existing PDF forms. SurveyJS sponsor 🤖 Top 10 Things AI Gets Wrong in Web Development — The Chrome team tested frontier coding agents and found they pass only about 50% of web best-practice checks unguided, but ~90% with Modern Web Guidance installed. The areas they get wrong include accessibility, performance and security. Philip Walton (Google) Introducing the Cross-Origin Storage API — A new API proposal from the Chrome team to enable sites to share large assets (like AI models, fonts, common libraries, etc.) meaning end users would save bandwidth by only having to download them once. Thomas Steiner ⚡️ IN BRIEF 🔦 jQuery 4.1 and 3.8 are out . 3.8 is the last planned feature release of the 3.x line, which now gets critical fixes only. 📑 Or perhaps you don't need jQuery at all? The long-standing ' You Don't Need jQuery ' guide has had a major update, swapping IE fallbacks for modern one-liners. 🌐 Chrome 158 is now stable , with the install element, media state pseudo-classes like :playing and :paused , and the start of XSLT's staged removal. Plus there's a look at what's new in the DevTools . ⛓️‍💥 A cautionary tale about using link shorteners: some old Bitly links were recently hijacked , repurposing where they sent people. 🌅 As we mentioned last month, Arc is going away on December 22, so Chris Coyier rounds up the browsers worth trying instead . 📙 Articles, Opinions & Tutorials Charts in HTML and CSS — A neat gallery of column and bar charts, heatmaps, donuts, line charts and more, built from just HTML and CSS (no JavaScript or SVGs). It's all built upon semantic markup, so if you strip away the stylesheet, they remain readable tables or lists. There's also an agent skill. Keith Cirkel Charts That Do Analytics? Yes, With One Script — Give your users forecasts and anomaly detection in the chart itself. Orbit for Highcharts, free for 60 days . Highcharts sponsor The CSS caret-* Properties and Custom Caret Accessibility — A thorough look at the newer caret-shape and caret-animation properties alongside caret-color for styling the text cursor. Covers caret browsing, WCAG rules, and how author styles can trump users' caret preferences. Sara Soueidan What Safari on Apple HomeView Means for Your Site — Safari now runs on Apple's square, 7-inch, voice-driven display. Most sites 'just work' but Jen flags some assumptions that break, like a shorter viewport than usual, an iOS user agent on a non-iPhone, and voice users who need labeled controls. Jen Simmons (WebKit) PropFLIP: Because It Flips with Props — Adam takes four @property custom properties and uses them, along with a transition, to create a neat flip effect. A sprinkling of JS helps bring it all together. Adam Argyle Giving AI Agents a Better Way to Debug CSS Amit Merchant Building an atproto Link Aggregator Johanna Larsson 🧰 Tools, Code & Resources Allo: Your Friendly Neighborhood Font — A really nice, free, open source typeface with variable weights and roundness options, automatic optical sizing, plenty of alternates, and much more. The site does an excellent job of showing it all off. Repo here . Josh Puckett 📊 Who Shipped First? Chromium vs Gecko vs WebKit — A look at 'which browser engine got there first' for a huge range of Web platform features. Patrick used the web-features data for this and Chromium/Chrome, perhaps unsurprisingly, has a clear lead in introducing new features. Patrick Brosset Your Chart Renders Fast. The Query Behind It Doesn’t — Tiger Cloud keeps dashboard queries fast as data grows, and it’s still Postgres underneath. $1000 credit to start . Tiger Data (creators of TimescaleDB) sponsor 🐞 BugShot: Chromium Extension for Streamlined Bug Reporting — Adds a side panel for turning browser bugs into a report that includes captures, annotations, recordings, and logs. It can then submit reports directly to Jira, GitHub, Linear, Notion, and more. SinhyeokKang Astrobook: A Minimal Storybook Alternative — An alternative to the popular Storybook UI component playground that supports React, Vue, Preact, Svelte, Solid, Lit, and Astro. The demo site includes multiple framework examples. Ocavue Aura: Ambient Gradients Built from Layered CSS Blend Modes — 200+ customizable gradients that offer a soft, atmospheric look that feels 'like light' . Click any gradient to preview it live, browse sub-categories (mesh, nebula, lattice, glass, etc.), and export as PNG, SVG, CSS, Tailwind, etc. GitHub repo . Cristian Olivera 📰 Classifieds ⚡️ Add lightning-fast 1D/2D barcode scanning to your web app with STRICH . On-device processing, free trial and demo! 📱 No Mac needed. Expo Simulators gives your coding agent a cloud iOS Simulator to test its own work, on Linux or Windows. 🧾 Generating invoices or reports from JSON? items.title: Introducing Vercel X
items.summary: Today we’re launching Vercel X , a six-week accelerator for AI founders at the idea and pre-seed stages. Join a cohort of 40 teams at our San Francisco HQ and build alongside Vercel’s product leaders, designers, and engineers. The program takes no equity for participation and offers access to a program-wide pool of more than $9M in credits from Vercel, AWS, Anthropic, OpenAI, and other partners. Applications are now open through November 29, 2026. The program runs from January 19 to March 2, 2027. Vercel has worked with more than 100 early-stage teams from around the world across three accelerator cohorts. Alumni include Rex , Alloy Robotics, Interfaze , Cervo , and Hacktron . Interfaze and Rex are backed by Y Combinator, and Cervo was acquired by Altana Technologies. Why Vercel X? If you’re applying to Vercel X, you probably have an idea or project you haven’t been able to stop thinking about. The next stretch is figuring out exactly what you’re building and who it’s for. We think you get through that stretch the Vercel way: by deeply understanding your customers, shipping quickly, and iterating to greatness. The program includes: Technical mentorship: Hands-on workshops and product feedback from Vercel’s design, product, and engineering teams. Partner credits: Put credits toward hosting, compute, and model API usage as you build and test your product. Founder community: A cohort of AI founders at the same stage, with weekly fireside chats featuring industry leaders. Investor access: Mentorship from VC partners and the opportunity to present your company to investors, ecosystem partners, and the Vercel community at Demo Day. Winning teams receive funding from Vercel Ventures and prizes from program partners. Who should apply We’re looking for technical builders with ambitious ideas and insatiable curiosity. You don’t need a finished product or traction. Tell us what you want to build, who needs it, what AI makes possible, and why you’re the right person or team for the job. Solo founders and teams of up to three can apply from around the world. You must be a Vercel customer and must not have participated in a traditional VC accelerator or raised an institutional seed round. See the additional eligibility requirements below. All participants must spend the full six weeks in San Francisco and attend weekly events in person. Apply to Vercel X Applications close at 11:59 p.m. PT on Sunday, November 29, 2026. Decisions will be released in mid-December. Apply to Vercel X → Applicants must be Vercel customers at or above the age of majority in their jurisdiction, able to commit to the full six weeks in person, and not located in or otherwise subject to restrictions imposed by U.S. sanctions laws. Vercel X program applications will be judged on the quality of the submission, the founder's background, and the overall potential for impact. Read more

Deploy a landing page with its stylesheet and images, or a report created by your coding agent, through the Vercel CLI or REST API . With the CLI, run: Newly supported file types include: Styles and data: CSS, JSON, XML, plain text, and web manifests Images: SVG, PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, AVIF, and ICO Fonts: WOFF, WOFF2, TTF, OTF, and EOT Documents and media: PDF, MP4, WebM, MP3, WAV, and OGG Instant deployments support up to 100 files totaling 25 MB or less. items.title: Introducing eve 1.0
items.summary: Today we're announcing eve 1.0 , the open-source framework for building production-ready agents. Since the public preview in June , we've worked with early adopters to prepare eve for 1.0, shipping 230+ releases and merging thousands of pull requests. With this release, eve is now generally available. We've made eve faster, expanded integrations, and improved observability. Security controls let you decide which actions need approval and what data gets collected. We've also made it easier for coding agents to build with, measuring that experience with a rigorous evaluation suite. With eve handling your harness and infrastructure, you and your agent can focus on building instead. Build production agents on a harness you own The harness in eve is the loop that calls models, runs tools, and delegates work to subagents. You choose the model, add or replace tools, edit instructions, and decide which actions need approval. The open-source Workflow SDK saves progress as the agent runs, so it can pick up from its last completed step after a crash. Multiplayer sessions and agent-to-agent calls are built in. For managed hosting, deploy your eve agent to Vercel. Vercel Workflows handles durable execution, and Vercel Sandbox runs agent-generated code in isolation. Build software factories that turn requests into tested pull requests, company brains that answer questions from your business data, or customer-facing agents in your product. Thousands of businesses already run eve in production for internal and customer-facing agents. Rillet built a software factory on eve that takes in customer requests, converts them into specs, tests the changes, and opens PRs for human review. Rillet tripled its shipping rate in three months. Clay built monty, a data agent that answers employees’ questions in Slack. Just over two months in, 30–40% of the company used it every week. Lindy 's agent framework roundup names eve “Best for durable backend agents”. Collaborate in multiplayer agent sessions Multiplayer lets several people work with an agent in one shared session. eve keeps track of who said what and directs approvals and sign-ins to the right person. You can set up memory for each user or the whole team. In the native Slack channel , each thread is one shared session. Approvals appear as buttons that only the right person can answer, and a live task card shows progress and timing. You can follow up in the thread without mentioning the agent again, cancel the current turn, or reset the session from Slack. Ambient mode lets an agent listen in channels you choose, even without being mentioned. Guided by goals you set per channel, it decides when to speak up, help, or take on a task, and when to stay quiet. To limit model costs, a small decision model screens every message first, and only the ones that might be for the agent start a turn. Slack is one of several native channels, alongside Microsoft Teams, Discord, Telegram, GitHub, Linear, Twilio, Web Chat, and iMessage. The Chat SDK channel adds support for any Chat SDK platform adapter, including WhatsApp, Messenger, Google Chat, and email. Each channel is one file, and the same agent can work across all of them. See the integrations directory for the full list. Build agent UIs with Next.js and other frameworks eve 1.0 expands our native integrations for Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit, TanStack Start, and Vite. The framework integrations build your agent alongside your app and set up its routes. On Vercel, you can deploy the agent and your site as one project, or host them separately. The client libraries let you work with tool calls, approval requests, and questions in a consistent way across frameworks. Use that session data to build custom UIs: stream replies into agent chats, embed an agent in a page, or show the agent's tool calls in your own components. Use eve add channel/web to scaffold a chat app with AI Elements components, or add eve's React, Vue, or Svelte bindings to an existing UI. Build multi-tenant agents One support-agent deployment can connect to each customer's ticketing system with their own credentials and apply that customer's approval rules. Your application authenticates the user and identifies which tenant they belong to. You can then set memory , connection credentials , and approval policy for that tenant and user. Before each model call in the main agent loop, dynamic definitions load the agent's capabilities from the session and external data. In 1.0, they cover models, connections, and subagents as well as tools, skills, and instructions. Give agents memory across sessions We added native memory so agents can carry context from one session to the next. You choose the memory's scope and can use the built-in file memory, a memory provider, or one you build yourself . Built-in fileMemory keeps data in memory in eve dev and in a private Vercel Blob store you configure on Vercel. Other providers include claude-mem , Hindsight , Kybernesis Arcana , Memanto , memco , Supermemory , and Upstash AgentKit . Trace agents with OpenTelemetry We rebuilt eve’s tracing around OpenTelemetry , so you can follow an agent’s work in the tracing tools you already use. eve dev records traces locally by default. If you host eve yourself, you can export them to an OpenTelemetry backend, including one you run yourself. Tracing integrations include Raindrop , with more options in the integrations directory . Add one with eve add instrumentation/ , or use the instrumentation APIs to build your own integration. Traces now show when an agent is waiting for a person, including tool approvals, questions, budget prompts, and sign-ins. They record model selections and approval decisions alongside model usage and cost, and follow calls into MCP servers and remote agents. You choose what eve collects for tracing. Content you exclude from collection stays out of every destination. You can filter out spans or redact inputs and outputs per destination. Private conversations in production send only metadata by default, without prompts or tool results. The OpenTelemetry guide explains these controls. On Vercel, Agent Runs uses the same traces to show sessions, model calls, tool execution, subagent activity, and approval decisions in the dashboard. When eve deploy creates a new Vercel project, it sets up trace sampling automatically. See the Agent Runs guide for setup and configuration. Lower agent turn latency At the start of September, our hosted stress test on Vercel Workflows took a median of 3.036s per turn . In 1.0, the same 100-turn workload took 414ms . The test sends messages one at a time, with one immediate mock-model response and no tool calls per turn. We measure from sending a message until the turn finishes, capturing eve and Workflow overhead without the time a model takes to generate a response. Hosted stress run Median turn latency p95 September 1, beta baseline 3.036s 3.692s November 15, 1.0.0 414ms 633ms We worked with the Workflow team on spec 9 , which gives each run a single orchestrator so background steps no longer replay the workflow. The team also moved event and stream writes to WebSockets and cut redundant history reads. eve agents get these improvements through Workflow SDK. eve also caches the information it needs to route messages to each session and can move idle sessions to a newer deployment between turns. Web UIs can prewarm a session before the first message arrives, so the first reply starts sooner. Lower workflow costs for long agent sessions For a 50-turn Evo Docs session, the estimated Vercel Workflows cost drops from 5.4¢ to 1.3¢, about 76% lower. That assumes roughly two model steps per turn and 30-day retention. eve now uses Workflow SDK 5.5 and saves only the conversation data that changed between turns. We've also cut repeated work in workflow steps, checkpoints, and sandbox setup: Workflow steps save changes and refer back to data already stored, instead of repeatedly copying a growing conversation into each step. Steps that don't need history no longer receive it. Checkpoints store references to image files returned by tools, so they don't have to copy the image bytes each time. Sandboxes from prepared snapshots skip repeated setup. Stop a sandbox and keep its files for reuse. Cleanup starts when the session ends. The storage changes are part of the open-source Workflow SDK, so agents you host yourself on other Workflow backends also store less duplicate session data. The cost estimate above uses Vercel Workflows pricing . On Vercel, workflow steps run on Fluid compute . They need extra storage writes for inputs above the payload size limit, so sending less session data helps keep turn times consistent as sessions grow. Images and files can still require those writes. For model calls, tool and skill listings can stay out of the initial prompt until they're needed. Connection tools run through eve__search and eve__tool , so each search no longer has to expand the model's tool list. We also changed how eve marks parts of a prompt for provider caching, so more content can be reused between calls. During an earlier migration to eve, an engineer at Evisions reported: Share agent capabilities with extensions Since the preview, we've added extensions so teams can share tools, skills, instructions, connections, channels, schedules, hooks, and subagents without copying files between agents. You can use extensions from the extensions directory or create your own with npx eve@latest extension init . For example, agent-browser adds browser automation, Mux Video adds tools for video assets and clips, and Link adds wallet and purchase tools. eve builds workspace extensions from source and reloads changes during development. You can update shared capabilities in one package and try the changes in your agents as you work. Build coding agents with eve’s shared tools The 1.0 code extension builds on eve’s default file tools, adding coding instructions and skills that follow your repository’s AGENTS.md . It's included in the eve package, so there's nothing extra to install. Give it a repository in its sandbox and your agent can investigate code, edit files, and run the project's checks. It uses the same harness and extension system as your other agents, so you can replace or disable tools, override skills, and add your own instructions. See the benchmark results for comparisons with other coding harnesses using the same tasks and model. Add the coding extension to your agent: The companion eve/extensions/git adds GitHub and pull request workflows, using credentials and authorization you configure. On Vercel, the optional remote self-modification extension lets your agent propose changes to its own source in a draft pull request. You review the changes, merge them, and deploy. Build with the same public APIs eve uses We built eve's subagents, sleep, and question tools on the same workflow system you can use through defineWorkflowTool . Your tools can return a result, start a background task, or keep accepting messages as a resumable task. They can wait for a person, webhook, or timer without keeping compute running, and their runs survive restarts. You don't need a separate background-job system to coordinate that work. Once you've defined a reviewer subagent, this tool returns a receipt immediately. The task body waits for the reviewer's result, which is delivered to the model in a later message: Upgrade to eve 1.0 If you already have an eve agent, the 1.0 upgrade guide walks through the changes to extension builds, agent APIs, session events, clients, and saved history. Follow it before deploying your upgrade. eve follows semantic versioning , so breaking changes to stable APIs only happen in major releases. Experimental and internal APIs, including experimental fields, can change between major releases. To work through the upgrade with your coding agent, copy this prompt: Create your first eve agent Start in the terminal to build locally, use the browser builder to create and deploy an agent, or choose a template for your use case. Start in the terminal Create a new agent from the CLI with Node.js 24 or newer: In an interactive terminal, this installs dependencies and opens the eve terminal UI. If your selected team has AI Gateway access, you can start chatting without creating a Vercel project or copying an API key. eve can use your existing Vercel CLI credentials to call models through AI Gateway locally. Use /login to sign in to other connections. In eve dev , you can ask the agent to add a tool, change its instructions, or write a skill. With self-modification , it edits its own source and reloads the change for the next turn. Start in the browser From the Vercel dashboard, the agent builder scaffolds an agent, creates its Git repo, and deploys it. Go to Add New → Agent, pick a model, and add web chat or Slack along the way. Start from a template Choose an eve template for your use case: Use case Templates Coding Coding agent · Software factory · GitHub maintainer · Incident response Knowledge and data Company brain · Data analyst · Shared files with Vercel Drives Apps and interfaces Next.js chat · TanStack Start chat · Voice agent · Agent with Python Messaging Slack · Discord · Personal agent · BELL Stack Memory Memory agent · Mem0 Content and marketing Contentful · Sanity copilot · Content agent · Marketing team Learn more in the eve docs . items.title: Decision-1.1 now available on AI Gateway
items.summary: Decision-1.1 from Microsoft AI is now available on AI Gateway. It is more accurate, better calibrated, and faster than Decision-1. The decision model returns structured answers instead of free-form text for tasks such as routing support requests, choosing which model should handle a request, selecting the next step in a workflow, or grading AI responses. Boolean: the probability that a condition is true Choice: a selected category and probabilities for each option Score: a numerical rating on a scale you define Multiple questions can share the same input in one request. Better calibration means the model's probabilities track how often it is right, so your application can set thresholds for when to act, flag a case for review, or escalate. Decision-1.1 accepts the same request format as Decision-1. To switch, change the model ID to microsoft/decision-1.1 . Call it through the AI SDK , the OpenAI-compatible Decisions API , or the AI CLI . The examples below require ai 7.0.128 or later for TypeScript, or the OpenAI Python SDK 3.26.0 or later for Python. Decision requests appear in request logs , count toward budgets , and support decision fallbacks . Try Decision-1.1 in the model playground , or see the decision models documentation for request formats and question types. Read more

For the API examples, set AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY to your AI Gateway API key . Both models also support the Responses API . To request Ultrafast, set providerOptions.openai.serviceTier to 'ultrafast' in the AI SDK, or set service_tier to 'ultrafast' in Chat Completions and Responses requests. GPT-6.2 Astra’s Ultrafast output-token price is 60% lower than GPT-6 Astra’s. To use the models in coding agents like Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup: Then select openai/gpt-6.2-astra or openai/gpt-6.2-sol in the agent. items.title: Hy4 Flash now available on AI Gateway for 50% off
items.summary: Hy4 Flash from Tencent is now available on AI Gateway with an introductory 50% discount on input, cached input, and output tokens through November 29, 2026. Hy4 Flash is the new lower-cost model in the Hy4 family. It keeps the full Hy4 feature set at roughly a tenth of the price per token: reasoning with preserved thinking across turns, tool calling, structured outputs, prompt caching, and image input, with the same 1M-token context window. Reasoning can be turned off for requests that don't need it, which suits high-volume coding, agent, and document workloads. Use tencent/hy4-flash as the model name: To use it in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup: Then select tencent/hy4-flash in the agent. See the coding agents guide for details. Try Hy4 Flash in the model playground . AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring retries, failover, and performance optimizations for higher-than-provider uptime. It includes built-in custom reporting , Zero Data Retention support , budgets for API keys , routing rules , and more. AI Gateway reflects provider pricing with no markup and does not charge a platform fee on inference, including on Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests. You can view all language models available on AI Gateway. Read more
